analysis.one_liner: Samvardhana Motherson makes auto parts for carmakers worldwide - wiring harnesses, mirrors, plastic modules - and is now pushing into aerospace and consumer electronics through acquisitions.
tags: Q1 FY26 profit fell 45% on tariff lag
analysis.whats_happening: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026) results showed PAT of ₹1,076 crore, up 77.5% YoY, on revenue of ₹35,244 crore (up 16.7%) - but that big jump is largely a base effect against a weak Q1 FY26 (see quarters note below). In September 2026 the company approved a ₹500.4 crore acquisition of 50.1% of Rotary Connectors (military-grade connectors, feeding its aerospace/defence push) and completed a restructuring that made Motherson Technology Services a wholly owned subsidiary. Q2 FY27 results are due around 14 November 2026, about four weeks from now.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a very large, very diversified auto-parts supplier that has grown mainly by buying other companies rather than just growing organically. The stock looks expensive on a P/E basis (high 30s) for a business whose return on equity (around 11%) is actually below the sector median - the tension is that the market is pricing in future growth from aerospace, electronics and new acquisitions, not current profitability. Revenue has grown steadily but profit has been lumpier quarter to quarter because of one-off costs like tariffs and new-plant startup expenses.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY26 (Apr-Jun 2025) profit fell 44.8% YoY to ₹606 crore despite revenue growth of 4.7%, which management blamed on a timing lag in passing on US tariff costs, FX volatility, and startup costs on new greenfield plants - not a demand problem. Q4 FY26 (Jan-Mar 2026) PAT rose 42.5% YoY to ₹1,497 crore. Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026) PAT of ₹1,076 crore up 77.5% YoY is flattered by that weak Q1 FY26 base - the two-year PAT path (₹1,097cr → ₹606cr → ₹1,076cr) shows recovery, not a clean acceleration. For FY26 overall, revenue crossed ₹1,26,104 crore (+11%) and EBITDA rose 11% to ₹12,033 crore, broadly tracking each other rather than one outrunning the other.
analysis.performance_read: The stock has done 9 stock splits (each roughly 3:2) since 2005, most recently in July 2025 - this explains why the price looks low (₹160) relative to its history; it is not value destruction, just more shares outstanding, and the returns below already account for this. Over 1 year the stock is up 49.9% versus Nifty -9.5% and peer Bosch +19.1%; over 3 years, up 150.5% versus Nifty +16.8% and Bosch +131.4%. Over 5 years, though, Motherson's 151.1% total return actually trails Bosch's 176.9%, so the recent 1-3 year outperformance versus this peer is a newer development, not a consistent multi-year trend. The stock is down 6.3% from its 31 August 2026 peak of ₹170.68, which is ordinary volatility, not a crash.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates across sources cluster between roughly 36x and 40x (one Screener-style source shows 39.91x against a sector median of 28.06x), with P/B around 4.1-4.2x versus a sector median of about 2.7x. It is expensive relative to peers on both counts. Why it is expensive: the market appears to be paying for the acquisition-led diversification into aerospace (revenue up 37% YoY in that segment) and consumer electronics (up 36%), plus the improved balance sheet. Whether that premium is justified is a separate question - ROE of ~11% is below the sector median of ~12.6%, so profitability has not yet caught up to the valuation multiple.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is a mix - revenue is rising from both volume (content per vehicle, new wins) and acquisitions (Atsumitec, Rotary Connectors), so it's not purely volume-led or purely margin-led. Within segments, profitability improvement is visible: polymer business margin rose from 6.4% to 7.4% sequentially, and emerging businesses margin improved 110 bps QoQ to 9.5%. Aerospace and consumer electronics are the fastest-growing but still small pieces of a much larger base dominated by traditional auto components.
analysis.health_read: Cash conversion looks solid: FY26 operating cash flow nearly doubled to ₹11,284 crore from ₹6,286 crore in FY25, and net leverage fell to an all-time low of 0.8x (D/E 0.39x) with net debt of ₹9,811 crore against ₹14,759 crore of liquidity. This points to financial risk being low; the real risk here is business/execution risk - integrating a steady stream of acquisitions and managing tariff/FX timing lags that have hit margins in the past (as in Q1 FY26).
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 48.6% (27.3% Indian promoters, 21.3% foreign promoters), broadly stable since mid-2025. Promoter pledge has been falling - 2.90% of promoter holding in March 2026 down to 2.34% by June 2026 - a small and shrinking figure, not a red flag by itself. Institutional ownership is spread across mutual funds (16.5%), FIIs (12.5%), insurance (3.3%) and DIIs (1.3%), with retail holding 17.8%. Not verified - no widely tracked individual marquee investor (the kind that shows up prominently in financial media) appears on the public shareholding list for this stock.
strengths: Net leverage at an all-time low of 0.8x (D/E 0.39x) with ₹14,759 crore of liquidity headroom for further acquisitions
FY26 operating cash flow nearly doubled to ₹11,284 crore from ₹6,286 crore in FY25
Aerospace (+37% YoY) and consumer electronics (+36% YoY) are scaling fast off a small base via targeted M&A like Rotary Connectors
Promoter pledge trending down (2.90% to 2.34% of promoter holding between March and June 2026)
watchpoints: ROE of ~11% sits below the auto-ancillary sector median of ~12.6% even as the stock trades at a P/E and P/B premium to that same sector
Margins have shown real sensitivity to timing lags on passing through costs - Q1 FY26 PAT fell 44.8% YoY on tariff pass-through delays and new-plant startup costs
Growth is substantially acquisition-dependent (Atsumitec, Rotary Connectors, Autoelectric, Shenzhen Autocruis among recent deals), which raises integration and capital-allocation risk over time
5-year total return (151.1%) still trails peer Bosch (176.9%), so the recent 1-3 year outperformance is not yet a long multi-year pattern
analysis.one_thing: Watch the Q2 FY27 results due around 14 November 2026, specifically whether the normalized PAT margin and segment-level margins (polymer, emerging businesses) hold their recent sequential improvement - that resolves whether Q1 FY27's 77.5% profit jump was a durable recovery or just a weak-base comparison.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked quarterly PAT/revenue figures (Q1 FY26, Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27) and FY26 full-year leverage/cash-flow figures across multiple independent sources (Angel One, HDFC Sky, Business Standard, company investor presentations) - these are consistent. Valuation ratios (P/E 35.7x-39.91x, ROE 10.77%-11.2%, ROCE 13.4%-13.63%) vary slightly by source and date; used the cluster range rather than a single point figure. Could not verify from public search whether any named marquee individual investor holds a disclosed stake - stated as not found rather than assumed absent with certainty. Q2 FY27 results date (14 Nov 2026) is sourced from a single secondary report and should be checked against the official NSE/BSE filing closer to the date.
